Course

Neural networks in t27: from one neuron to a transformer block

The agents of this project think with neural networks, and here their parts are written as t27 specs with tests, specs the compiler checks. Every widget runs the fn bodies of a specs/ml spec compiled to WebAssembly: move a slider and the spec answers.

Course 10, 27 lessons, a live widget and a t27 spec each: activations, softmax and embeddings, pooling and batch norm, losses, SGD, RMSProp and Adam, backpropagation and XOR, recurrent cells, attention, a transformer block and PPO. Every number is computed by a compiled spec.

All lessons

  • Module 1 · One neuron

    A neuron sums its inputs and bends the sum: ReLU, the sigmoid and tanh, and where each one stops passing a gradient back.

    1. 01 ReLU: keep the positive part
    2. 02 The sigmoid: a number into a probability
    3. 03 tanh and saturation

  • Module 2 · New bends

    The smooth curves of current models: GELU with its dip, Swish with its knob, and ELU with a floor instead of a cliff.

    1. 04 GELU: a dip below zero
    2. 05 Swish and SiLU
    3. 06 ELU: a floor, not a cliff

  • Module 3 · A layer

    What sits around the neurons: softmax turns scores into a choice, an embedding turns a word into numbers, dropout switches units off.

    1. 07 Softmax and temperature
    2. 08 Embeddings
    3. 09 Dropout

  • Module 4 · Pictures

    Reading a picture in patches: a window averaged over its patch, max pooling, and batch normalisation of features on different scales.

    1. 10 Patches of a picture
    2. 11 Max pooling
    3. 12 Batch normalisation

  • Module 5 · The error

    How wrong a guess is, as one number: mean squared error, cross-entropy for probabilities, and the Huber loss for outliers.

    1. 13 Mean squared error
    2. 14 Cross-entropy
    3. 15 The Huber loss

  • Module 6 · Downhill

    Walking down the loss: gradient descent with momentum, RMSProp that ignores the gradient's size, and Adam that combines them.

    1. 16 Gradient descent
    2. 17 RMSProp
    3. 18 Adam

  • Module 7 · Learning

    Where the gradients come from and what they achieve: backpropagation through a layer, a network that learns XOR, and LAMB for large batches.

    1. 19 Backpropagation
    2. 20 Learning XOR
    3. 21 LAMB and large batches

  • Module 8 · Memory and attention

    Networks that read a sequence: a recurrent cell and its fading echo, the gates of an LSTM, and attention over every position at once.

    1. 22 A recurrent cell
    2. 23 LSTM gates
    3. 24 Attention

  • Module 9 · The transformer and the reward

    The parts of a transformer and of an agent: positions as clocks, one encoder block, and PPO, which learns from reward without lurching.

    1. 25 Positional encoding
    2. 26 An encoder block
    3. 27 PPO and the reward
